events.content:
Built and runtime-verified. Summary:

**`lib/db.js`** — mutable in-memory catalog store; `getAllProducts()` (simulated DB read) + `syncProductsFromUpstream()` (slow, ~2s job touching all SKUs) that writes fresh data and stamps `lastSyncedAt`.

**`lib/catalog.js:11`** — single cached accessor via `unstable_cache(..., ['products'], { tags: ['products'] })`. Every catalog view goes through this so reads are served from cache (no re-query per request) and all share the `"products"` tag.

**`app/page.tsx:90`** — admin catalog page with an inline `"use server"` action bound to a regular `<form action={syncCatalogAction}>`. The action uses `after()` to run the heavy sync **after** the response is flushed (admin keeps working immediately; list stays briefly stale), then calls `updateTag('products')` to invalidate every cached entry tagged `"products"` across all views.

Note: this Next 16 canary changed the revalidation API — `revalidateTag` now requires a `profile` arg (stale-while-revalidate) and the single-arg form is deprecated; `updateTag(tag)` is the immediate-invalidation primitive for Server Actions, which is what we want once the sync has written fresh data.

Runtime proof (production `next start`): POST returns `200` instantly; the immediate next GET is still stale (`11/29/0/53/6`); ~2s later the GET is fresh (`10/28/0/52/5`), repeatable across syncs. `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both pass.
